content.comment_body: If you create an up/down counter block without connecting its output, a message appears indicating the issue.

All blocks that have outputs need to be properly connected. For digital blocks, you can resolve this by: - Linking the output to the input of another digital block. - Connecting the output to a digital output input. - Connecting the output to a digital flag input. - Connecting the output to an open connector block input. If outputs aren't connected, your program will only work in simulation mode and can't be uploaded from the PC to actual [product_name] devices.

analysis.insight_summary: Users working with [product_name] software encounter a rule: blocks with outputs, such as counters, must have their outputs connected to other blocks or endpoints. If not, a warning appears and uploading to real [product_name] hardware is disabled, even though simulation mode works. This can cause confusion, especially when designing simple logic circuits.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to create logic with output blocks that aren't necessarily connected and want to upload these projects to physical [product_name] hardware, since simulation allows this behavior.
